_comment: Hotspots where a spotting scope changes what you can identify — open water,
a long tide flat, a distant sandspit. Binoculars still get you there; the
scope is what turns a distant smudge into a species.
This is the MANUAL tier of backlog F19, and it is deliberately first: a
hand-listed site is perfectly precise about the places you already know,
costs no API calls, and cannot mis-flag anything. The automatic detector
(taxon fraction — what share of a site's records are waterfowl, loons,
grebes, alcids and distant shorebirds) is tier 2 and is NOT what this file
is. Adding a site here is a two-line edit and needs no code change.
Keyed by eBird locId because a hotspot NAME is not stable — eBird renames
and merges them, and the same name can exist in several counties.
Shared byte-identical between the report and the app (the parity suite
compares them exactly), so a site flagged in one is flagged in both.
`why` is rendered to the reader, so write it as a reason rather than a
label: 'the birds are on the far side of open water' tells you whether to
bother carrying the tripod; 'scope site' does not.

L164858.name: Jetty Island
L164858.why: shorebirds and terns work the far tide flats and the outer spit — most of the birds are beyond binocular range at low tide

L936924.name: Edmonds Fishing Pier
L936924.why: loons, grebes, scoters and alcids sit well out on Puget Sound; from the pier the interesting birds are usually the distant ones
